elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 reads: "This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York." The prior Singapore governing-law words are gone.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Retained 28.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction..." The competing exclusive Singapore forum words in 28.1 were deleted, so exclusivity is no longer contradicted.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. The fallback is intentionally not the chosen level (the comment merely offers it in negotiation).

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The operative forum is the state and federal courts in New York County; no Delaware, California, or London forum appears.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: 28.1 now designates New York law and retained 28.2 supplies exclusive state and federal jurisdiction in New York County, matching both preferred elements in operative language rather than in the comment.

Minimal: the edit touches only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 and deletes the conflicting exclusive Singapore forum, which was necessary to make the New York County exclusivity in 28.2 operative. No survival tails, procedures, arbitration carve-outs, or other extras were added.

Preserves intent: 28.2's submission to personal jurisdiction, venue/inconvenient-forum waiver, and the injunctive-relief carve-out survive unchanged; the 28.3 escalation mechanic and all cross-references remain intact, and no defined term (e.g., Confidential Information) is left dangling.
Fallback level is correctly not satisfied and need not be — the redline sits at the preferred position, and the comment offers Delaware/California/England and Wales only as a negotiation fallback.
Note only (not a defect): 28.1 drops the word "exclusively" from the governing-law sentence; this is immaterial because choice of law is stated affirmatively and forum exclusivity is carried by 28.2.
